Commentary.Commentary: Rain intervened again with Afghanistan 8 down for 96. Zimbabwe though did not take long after resumption and bowled them out for 111. Asghar Stanikzai was the top scorer for them and it tells you how well Zimbabwe have bowled. Mpofu was the best bowler for the hosts, taking 3/25 while Chatara, Rashid chipped in with a couple of wickets each. They have a modest total to chase and will back their team to chase down this total and set it up for the final game. Join us in a while for the chase.

All over! Afghanistan have been bowled out for 111. Gulbadin Naib was run out for 5 and Rashid Khan was the last man to fall. They will be disappointed with the way they have batted in this game. Yes, the conditions were overcast and the hosts bowlers were brilliant right throughout the game. Tendai Chatara and Chris Mpofu who set it up for Zimbabwe, reducing Afghanistan to 46 for 5. The lower order did try to hang around but the spin of Graeme Cremer was good enough to dismiss the two relatively set batsmen.
OUT c Graeme Cremer b Chris Mpofu. Afghanistan have been bowled out.
OUT Gulbadin Naib run out (Malcolm Waller). Afghanistan have lost their ninth wicket.

After 36 overs, Afghanistan are 100/8. It is bright and sunny now. The visitors will be hoping to make most of the six overs left in their innings. 100 up for them but they will know, they need to get a lot more runs in here. Zimbabwe will aim to wrap up the game as early as possible.

1343 local time- Good news! The covers have been peeled off. We should have a word on the resumption time and also on the status of the overs left for this inning. We have lost only 8 overs. It will be a 42 overs per side game. So, Afghanistan are batting. Rashid Khan to continue with Gulbadin Naib.
1300 local time - The rain has finally stopped. The umpires are having a look and the covers are being peeled off slowly.

1228 local time - Rain is back! After 34.4 overs, Afghanistan are 96/8! Solomon Mire is called back into the attack and he strikes immediately having Mohammad Nabi caught by Craig Ervine for 17. Afghanistan are falling apart here and the rain is back to halt the progress of the hosts.
OUT c Craig Ervine b Solomon Mire. Afghanistan have lost their eighth wicket.
Good news! The covers are coming off. The game will be restarting soon. Stay tuned for more updates.

Oh dear! The rains are here! After 32 overs, Afghanistan are 89/7. The pair of Nabi and Naib are looking to get the visitors back in the game with a stand but just as we say that, the rain that was forecast has arrived and the covers are on the field. Let's hope it clears up soon.

After 30 overs, Afghanistan are 85/7.  Looks we jinxed Afghanistan, just as we applauded them for a good stand, they have lost a couple of wickets. Shenwari top edged his slog sweep to short fine leg for a good catch to that man, Chatara again. Cremer then struck again to get rid of Karim Janat, who also was caught behind for 9. Mohammad Nabi and Mohammad Naib are battling it out there for the visitors.
OUT c Peter Moor b Graeme Cremer. Afghanistan have lost their seventh wicket.
OUT c Tendai Chatara b Graeme Cremer. Afghanistan have lost their sixth wicket.

After 25 overs, Afghanistan are 66/5. A good period of play for them as both Karim and Shenwari both have done well to stitch a stand here. There is a bit of rain around but the visitors will hope these two can carry on the good work. Graeme Cremer has bowled a superb spell so far, he has figures of 5-1-6-0!

After 20 overs, Afghanistan are 56/5! The visitors have now lost have their side with not much on the board. May be they are competing with India, who were bowled out for 105 in their first innings against Australia in Pune earlier today. Coming to the wicket, H Shahidi was out caught behind by Peter Moor. Shamiullah Shenwari has come out to bat. Both he and Karim have been watchful for now.
OUT c Peter Moor b Chris Mpofu. Afghanistan have lost their fifth wicket.

After 15 overs, Afghanistan are 44/4! Zimbabwe remain on top. The visitors scored 29 runs in four overs before losing the wicket in the last over. First boundary of the game came off the bat of Shahidi. Stanikzai too joined in to counterattack with a six. The runs started to flow for the visitors and hence Chris Mpofu was called on for a bowl and he struck with his very first ball, getting Asghar Stanikzai caught behind by Peter Moor. Karim Janat is the new man in.
OUT c Peter Moor b Chris Mpofu. Afghanistan have lost their fourth wicket.

After 10 overs, Afghanistan are 12/3! Zimbabwe are right on top here. Ihsanullah making his ODI debut had to depart for a 20-ball duck to Chatara who came back to dismiss Rahmat Shah for 1. Mohammad Shahzad was given a life when he was dropped at point but it was Richard Ngarva who got rid of him, having him caught at short mid-wicket, attempting a heave. Afghanistan skipper Asghar Stanikzai, is out in the middle with Hashmatullah Shahidi and they need a stand here.
OUT c Ryan Burl b Richard Ngarava. Afghanistan have lost their third wicket.
OUT b Tendai Chatara. Afghanistan have lost their second wicket.
OUT c Tarisai Musakanda b Tendai Chatara. Afghanistan have lost their first wicket.

After 5 overs, Afghanistan are 3/0. The openers have been circumspect for them and are intent to seeing off the two new balls. Mohammad Shahzad is known for his explosive batting but he has curbed his instincts so far. Ihsanullah making his ODI debut is yet to get off the mark.

The game is about to begin! Mohammad Shahzad and Ihsanullah are out to bat. Zimbabwe begin with Tendai Chatara. Unfortunately, due to lack of television feed, there won't be ball-by-ball commentary for this match but we shall keep you posted with updates.
Team changes - Afghanistan have made three changes. N Zadran, Amir Hamza, N Ali are out for Karim Janat, Ihsanullah and H Shahidi. Zimbabwe are unchanged from the previous game.
TOSS - Afghanistan win the toss and elect to bat!

The bowlers have had the upper hand for both the teams in the series and the trend is likely to continue with overcast conditions and a two-paced deck on offer. There is forecast for rain later in the day but let's hope that we get an uninterrupted game. The visitors will be hoping to seal the deal today itself while the hosts may have other ideas.

Hello everyone and welcome to the coverage of the fourth ODI between Zimbabwe and Afghanistan at the Harare Sports Club, Harare. The hosts have managed to stay alive in the series thanks to sensational bowling performances by Chris Mpofu and Sean Williams in the previous encounter. Afghanistan lost 5 wickets for 5 runs to lose the game and it makes the series a bit more interesting.
